title: Forensic proofworkflows and approval checks (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note outlines a pragmatic playbook for packaging and validating forensic evidence when customer-managed network changes are approved for Private deployments. It focuses on: 1) evidence bundle structure, 2) approval checkpoints and SLOs, 3) sampling and retention strategy, 4) operator UX and automation hooks, 5) emergency rollback indicators.

Context and problem statement:
Customer-managed networking (VPC peering, firewall policies, routing, outbound proxies) is the highest source of operational incidents after initial private handoff. Our current approval flow records basic audit entries but lacks standardized, machine-readable evidence bundles that downstream SREs, auditors, and customers can consume for postmortem and compliance. That gap slows troubleshooting and increases mean time to repair during network incidents.

Goals (measurable):
- Define a canonical "evidence bundle" JSON/text envelope that is produced at approval time and stored with immutable retention metadata.
- Add two non-blocking but observable checkpoints + one blocking approval gate for high-risk changes.
- Establish sampling policy so 100% of blocking approvals get full bundles; 10% of low-risk approvals get full bundles for regression analysis.
- Ensure a signed cryptographic receipt (operator assertion) is produced for all blocking approvals and kept for at least 1 year.
- Provide a lightweight developer/operator UX for evidence inspection (CLI + Console quickview).

Evidence bundle (high level):
- Bundle ID (UUID v4)
- Change metadata: change_id (ticket), customer_id, tenant_id, change_type (eg: firewall/route/peering), risk_score (0-100), requested_by, approver_id(s), change_window
- Snapshot artifacts: customer-src (diff of requested change), rendered-config-before, rendered-config-after, BGP/routing-announce-snapshot (if relevant), security-group-objects, NAT table snapshot
- Telemetry captures: connectivity-probe-results (pre/post), traceroute collection (3 samples), tcpdump snippet (first 256KB) if the customer permits, backend health sample (service-check responses)
- Approval statements: operator-assertion (base64-sig), approval-policy-version, canary-coverage-intent, rollback-plan-id
- Immutable metadata: created_at (ISO8601), created_by (service principal), retention-policy-id, evidence-hash (sha256)
- Forensic pointers: s3://immutable-bucket/<bundle-id>.tar.gz, signed-manifest-url, object-store-checksum

Notes on privacy: customer telemetry that includes PII MUST be redacted according to the customer agreement. The bundle should include a redaction manifest listing removed fields.

Operator assertion (format proposal):
- assertion = base64( sign(private_key_of_operator, canonicalized_evidence_manifest) )
- canonicalized_evidence_manifest fields: bundle_id, change_id, timestamp, approver_id, risk_score, short_hash_of_snapshot
- We will support operator keys stored in HSM/KMS and use an Audit key that is rotated quarterly.

Approval checkpoints and policy tiers:
- Low risk (policy tag: L0): non-blocking approval by standard operator or automated policy engine. Produce minimal audit log; optionally create evidence bundle per sampling policy (10%).
- Medium risk (L1): non-blocking but requires explicit human approval from a network operator. Evidence bundle created and attached to the ticket.
- High risk (L2): blocking approval required, must include operator assertion (signature) and a verified pre-change connectivity probe. Full evidence bundle mandatory.

SLOs and metrics to record at each checkpoint:
- Approval latency (ms): target median < 5 minutes for L1, < 15 minutes for L2 during business hours.
- Evidence artifact generation time: target < 30s for minimal bundle, < 2m for full bundle (asynchronous background allowed but must be completed before final commit for L2).
- Bundle integrity verification time: < 10s on retrieval.
- Sampling coverage: track percentage of low-risk approvals with full bundles (target 10% with 2% absolute tolerance).

Sampling strategy:
- Deterministic sampling using hash(change_id, customer_id, month) % 100 < sampling_pct to ensure reproducibility across retries.
- Override flag for manual QA to force-generation for investigation.

Retention and immutable storage:
- Evidence bundles for L2: retain for 3 years by default (customer contract override allowed).
- L1 bundles: 1 year. L0 sampled bundles: 90 days.
- All bundles written to an immutable object store with versioning and WORM-like semantics (GCS/Azure immutable buckets or S3 with Object Lock).

Runbook snippets (quick actions):
- On suspicion of regression after change commit:
  1) Pull bundle: CLI: ri private bundle get <bundle-id> --save /tmp/bundle.tgz
  2) Verify signature: ri private bundle verify <bundle-id>
  3) Run quick-diff: ri private bundle diff-configs <bundle-id> --before-after
  4) Run pre/post probes from our diagnostics host toward the customer endpoint as documented in the bundle.
- On missing artifacts: escalate to evidence-ingest team with copy of ticket and request id. We should have an ingest correlation id in every audit log.

Automation and hooks:
- Evidence generation endpoint: POST /private/changes/<change_id>/evidence-generate -> returns bundle-id (idempotent).
- Webhook subscription: customers and internal teams can subscribe to bundle-ready events (signed url + signed-manifest).
- Async job that uploads additional telemetry (tcpdump, traceroutes) to the bundle after commit; mark as 'supplemental' in the manifest.

Failure modes and mitigation:
- Evidence generation failure: retry exponential backoff X3, then mark change as "evidence-failed" and attach minimal diagnostics to ticket. For L2 changes, block final commit until resolved or manual override recorded with justification.
- Signature verification failure on retrieval: treat as potential tamper. Escalate to security and freeze related change rollouts.
- Storage unavailability: write to local encrypted archive and enqueue to object-store; ensure signed receipt is still produced so there's a recoverable chain.

Customer consent surfaces:
- Provide consent checkbox during initial customer onboarding and a contract clause for collection of tcpdump / packet-level captures. Default is no packet capture; only metadata and flow-level telemetry.

Example minimal manifest (human readable excerpt):
---
bundle_id: 7d8f3e2a-xxxx
change_id: JIRA-PD-987
customer_id: cust-2019
change_type: firewall-rule-add
risk_score: 62
approver_id: daniel.park@redwood.ai
created_at: 2026-02-25T16:02:12Z
evidence_artifacts:
  - rendered-config-before: s3://immutable/7d8f3e2a/before.txt
  - rendered-config-after: s3://immutable/7d8f3e2a/after.txt
  - connectivity-probe: s3://immutable/7d8f3e2a/probe-20260225.json
signature: base64(...)
---

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Decide canonical JSON schema for the full bundle (schema draft vs avro vs protobuf). I lean protobuf for compactness but JSON schema is easier for early adopters. (owner: Miguel)
- Where to store operator public keys for quick verification in the console? (KMS vs public key directory) (owner: Priya)
- Define redaction rules and automated PII scanner for packet/telemetry (owner: Aisha)
- Integration test for "missing artifact" path (owner: SRE team)

User experience notes (console + cli):
- Console: quickview shows bundle id, risk score, timeline, and 3 actionable buttons (verify, download, start rollback plan).
- CLI: simple one-liners to fetch/verify/diff. The CLI must not download packet captures unless --include-packets flag is set.

Stakeholders to review: product-private-deployments, eng-infrastructure, eng-sre, security, legal (for retention/consent), solutions-eng.

Appendix: short example approval flow (L2) steps for canary-enabled private deploy:
1) Ticket created with change request and intended canary coverage (10%).
2) Pre-change probes executed from Redwood canary agents -> results attached.
3) Operator reviews diffs and signs assertion with HSM-backed key.
4) Evidence bundle generated and written to immutable store.
5) System performs canary rollout; monitoring reads bundle for rollback-plan-id if anomaly detected.
6) If anomaly crosses threshold, rollback plan is executed; evidence bundle used for postmortem and forensics.

Notes-to-self (rough):
- Keep this doc narrow: focus on the "bundle + approval gate" contract. Separate doc for console UX and retention SLA.
- Reconcile with existing attestation-ledger PRD (CONF-4521) to avoid duplication.

-- end of draft --
